title: Dundee Cake
subtitle: a rich, lightly spiced Scottish fruit cake with almonds on top
excerpt: Dundee cake is lighter than a traditional Christmas cake -- less fruit, less dense, and no marzipan or icing. The blanched almonds pressed into the top in concentric circles are its signature. It is a proper keeping cake and improves with age.
sourceNotes: A Scottish classic, associated with Dundee. Claimed to have been first produced by the Keiller marmalade company in the 19th century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap in foil and freeze. Defrost overnight at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps for 2 to 3 weeks in an airtight tin. The flavour improves after a few days.
recipe.temperatureNote: Conventional oven -- low temperature for slow, even baking

content.text: Press the blanched almond halves into the surface in neat concentric rings before the cake goes in the oven. They will toast gently to a golden colour as the cake bakes. Line the tin with a double layer of baking paper, and tie a double layer of newspaper around the outside -- this prevents the edges from over-baking during the long cook.

items.prepNote: use 50g blanched almonds, halved, to decorate the top

content.text: Heat the oven to 150C. Grease and double-line a deep 20cm round tin with baking paper.
Beat the butter and brown sugar together for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs, one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, spices, orange and lemon zest, and milk. Stir in the currants and sultanas.
Spoon into the tin and level the top. Arrange the blanched almond halves over the surface in concentric circles.
Bake for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. If the top is browning too quickly, cover with foil. Cool in the tin completely before removing.

items.cause: Oven too hot, or no protective foil used.
items.fix: At 150C this should not happen, but if your oven runs hot, tent loosely with foil after the first hour.

items.cause: Over-baked -- fruit cakes dry out quickly once past their point.
items.fix: Test from 1 hour 45 minutes onwards. Remove as soon as the skewer is clean.

content.text: Dundee cake is one of Scotland's most distinctive contributions to British baking. It sits between an everyday fruit cake and a ceremonial Christmas cake in richness. It is cut in thick slices and eaten with butter or strong tea. The almond-decorated top is its most recognisable feature -- it appears on no other British cake in quite the same way.
